001: I've read the employee handbook and I have a question about remote work.
Sure, go ahead. That policy was updated last month.
How many days a week can we work from home?
At most three, but you need your manager's approval.
Got it. And is the schedule still flexible?
Yes, as long as you complete your weekly hours and attend the key meetings.
002: I've heard there's a new protocol for requesting vacation time.
That's right, now everything is done through the internal platform.
And how far in advance do I have to request it?
At least fifteen days in advance, except in cases of force majeure.
Okay, I'll keep that in mind when planning my next break.
Sounds good. If you need help with the system, let me know, no problem.
003: Do you know if the company covers the costs of external training?
It depends on the course and on whether it's related to your position.
I'm interested in one on data analysis. Who should I contact?
You have to send the proposal to the human resources department.
Perfect, I'll prepare a document with the details and the benefits.
Good idea. The clearer the objective is, the easier it will be to approve.
004: I saw that they've changed the policy on using personal devices.
Yes, now it's restricted for cybersecurity reasons.
Can we use our personal laptop to check email?
No, for that you must always use the equipment provided by the company.
I understand, that way confidential information is better protected.
Exactly. It's a necessary measure to prevent data leaks.
005: How does the new performance evaluation system work?
Now it includes a self-assessment and a quarterly meeting with your supervisor.
And are the goals set at the beginning of the year?
Yes, but they can be reviewed if the project context changes.
That seems like a very reasonable and flexible approach to me.
Me too. This way the process ends up being fairer for everyone.
006: I have a question about the travel expense policy.
Go ahead, what exactly do you need to know?
What expenses can I include when I travel for work?
Transportation, accommodation, and meals, as long as you keep the receipts.
And what's the daily limit for food?
It's forty euros per day, not including justified business dinners.
007: I've heard the company is going to implement a pay equity policy.
Yes, it's an initiative they had been preparing since last year.
How are they going to make sure it's effective?
They'll carry out internal audits and publish annual reports on the differences.
That seems like a very important step for transparency.
Definitely, it's a sign that the corporate culture is changing.
008: Is volunteering allowed during working hours?
Yes, the company offers eight hours a month for charitable activities.
And do I have to notify my team in advance?
Of course, to organize the work well and avoid setbacks.
I think it's great that the company supports these causes.
Me too, it's one of the policies I value the most.
009: I'm not clear on how the confidentiality policy with clients works.
It's very simple: no information is shared without explicit authorization.
And what if a client asks us for data from another project?
In that case, you must always check with your direct supervisor.
Alright, I'd rather err on the side of caution in these matters.
Without a doubt, it's better to prevent than to regret an information leak.
010: What do you think about the new work-life balance policy?
I think it's a big step forward, especially the extension of paternity leave.
Yes, now it's ten weeks, right?
Exactly, and it can also be taken in separate periods during the first year.
That gives families a lot more flexibility.
Totally, it shows that the company takes its employees' well-being seriously.
